decision: Reject repaired READY generation 2 before provider creation and require the owner to preserve and retrieve each paid stage under one continuous claim.

fixed_from_generation_1: matching exact-runner stage and invocation path

observed_blockers.evidence: The remote script proceeds directly from capture file-existence tests into training. No controller-local capture terminal or manifest is retrieved before the later consumer starts, despite the READY claim.
The owner never copies CAPTURE_TERMINAL.json, chunks.jsonl, head_checkpoint.pt, or HOLDOUT_RESULT.json to the controller; it writes a local success terminal solely from remote return code.

After any science marker is observed, the exception path raises immediately, stops the heartbeat in finally, writes no decision-bearing or repair terminal, and does not release. This leaves the claimed bench without a durable owner.

The packet and hashes are built once before the generation loop. repair_wait consumes REPAIR_REQUEST.json but neither validates its bound changes nor rebuilds the packet or command graph, so every retry restages the same bytes.

preserve: all immutable scientific bindings and hashes
the exact checkpoint, image, c32 workload, 4096/512 split, 16.054-token gate, and single capture/train/holdout cycle
the corrected server entrypoint, staged exact-runner path, health gate, and pre-request science marker
required_changes: Split capture and training into separately supervised stages.
After capture completes, retrieve and validate its compact terminal and manifest on the controller before training; preserve the remote content-addressed tap chunks.
If capture submission state is unknown, retrieve the marker, driver output, server log, and capture terminal before deciding whether any operation may resume.

If capture is complete and training or holdout consumption fails, keep the owner and heartbeat live, expose a fresh repair generation, and resume only the training/holdout consumer from the preserved capture.
Retrieve and validate HOLDOUT_RESULT.json plus the trained-head content identity before writing a local successful OWNER_TERMINAL.json or releasing.
Make a repair request executable: validate its hash-bound mutable files, rebuild the packet and command graph inside the corresponding generation, and record the predecessor repair ID.
Never stop the heartbeat or leave the claim ownerless without a decision-bearing terminal, unsafe/unreachable guest evidence, or absolute-deadline handoff.
Atomically replace H200_CAPTURE_TRAIN_READY.json with the corrected owner sha256 and this director-repair sha256.
